assessment.title: Homework #5 · MOSFET circuits at DC
assessment.topic: Module 5 · MOSFET DC bias · Diode-connected devices · Mirrors · CMOS
assessment.instructions: Show key steps, assumptions, and final answers with units. Use the long-channel square law with λ = 0: saturation I_D = ½k′(W/L)V_OV² for V_DS ≥ V_OV; triode I_D = k′(W/L)[V_OV·V_DS − V_DS²/2]. Always state and verify the region of every transistor. Enter numbers in the units shown.

questions.title: 1) Saturation drain current: scaling factors
questions.promptHtml:
An n-channel MOSFET is biased in saturation (long-channel, λ = 0).

(a) For each independent change, find the multiplicative factor by which ID changes:

  1. L is doubled.
  2. W is doubled.
  3. VOV = VGS − Vt is doubled.
  4. VDS is doubled.
  5. Changes (1)–(4) are applied simultaneously.

(b) Which change(s) could cause the MOSFET to leave saturation? Explain the mechanism.
hints: I_D = ½k_n′(W/L)V_OV² in saturation with λ = 0.
checklist: Check V_DS ≥ V_OV after each change.

responseFields.label: (b) Which change(s) can push the device out of saturation, and why?

questions.title: 2(a) Diode-connected NMOS: choose R for V_D = 0.8 V
questions.promptHtml:
NMOS Q1 is diode-connected (gate tied to drain) with its source at ground. Resistor R connects the drain to VDD = 1.8 V. Choose R so that VD = 0.8 V.

Given Vtn = 0.5 V, μnCox = 0.4 mA/V2, W/L = 0.72/0.18, λ = 0.
hints: V_GS = V_DS = V_D: a conducting diode-connected MOSFET is always in saturation.
checklist: Find I_D from the square law.

questions.title: 3) Node voltages in four MOSFET circuits
questions.promptHtml:
The four circuits (a)–(d) use identical transistors with |Vt| = 2 V, k′(W/L) = 1 mA/V2, λ = 0 (square law, ID = ½k′(W/L)VOV2 in saturation). Find the labeled node voltages V1 through V7.

Labels used here: (a) V1 = source, V2 = drain; (b) V3; (c) V4 = drain (also report the source voltage VS,c); (d) V5 = V6 = the node joining the drain and gate of the upper PMOS to the source of the lower PMOS, V7 = drain of the lower PMOS.
hints: Current sources fix I_D; then find V_GS from the square law — but always check the region.
In (c) and (d), the saturation assumption fails: solve the triode equation I_D = k′(W/L)[V_OV·V_DS − V_DS²/2].
checklist: Check V_DS ≥ V_OV; if it fails, re-solve in triode.

questions.title: 4) Two stacked diode-connected NMOS
questions.promptHtml:
Two identical long-channel NMOS transistors Q1 and Q2 are connected in series. A 1 kΩ resistor connects +5 V to node V1. Q1 runs from V1 (drain) to V2 (source); Q2 runs from V2 (drain) to V3 (source), and V3 is grounded. Each gate is tied to its own drain.

Vt = 1 V, k′(W/L) = 5 mA/V2, λ = 0 (ignore body effect). Find V1, V2, V3, and the current I.
hints: Both transistors carry the same current and are diode-connected, so they have the same V_GS.
V₂ = V_GS and V₁ = 2V_GS; write KCL through the 1 kΩ resistor.

questions.promptHtml:

hints: (a) The circuit is symmetric: try v_O = 0.
(b) Q_p has V_SG = 0 and is off; Q_n has V_GS = 5 V and must sink the load current — check whether it is in triode.
checklist: Find each device's V_GS (V_SG) and V_OV.
In (b) write KCL at v_O with the triode equation.

questions.title: 8) Circuit Studio · Load line, Q-point and tolerance spread of a degenerated bias
questions.promptHtml:
Circuit Studio problem · Load line & Q-point lens and Spread lens. Simulation tools are switched on for this question. Record each prediction before you use the tool that checks it.

The divider-bias circuit of Problem 6 with RS = 2 kΩ: VDD = 5 V, RG1 = RG2 = 1 MΩ, RD = 2 kΩ, RS = 2 kΩ, Vt = 1 V, kn = 2 mA/V², λ = 0.

  1. Predict: find ID by hand and confirm saturation.
  2. Open Visual Aids ▾ → Load line & Q-point and click M1. Record the Q-point VDS and the load line's current intercept (VDS = 0). Explain where the intercept comes from.
  3. Change kn to 4 mA/V² (in the Solution tab, under the circuit values and MOSFET model). Watch the Q-point move along the load line, and record the new ID and the percentage change.
  4. Set kn back to 2 mA/V². Open Visual Aids ▾ → Spread, choose ±5% Standard, and record the range of the drain voltage VD.
  5. Explain: why the bias moves so little when kn doubles, and what the Spread result means for a design that must keep VDS above VOV.
hints: V_G = 2.5 V and V_GS = V_G − I_D·R_S; keep the root with V_GS > V_t.
The drain–source loop is V_DD in series with R_D + R_S.
checklist: Q-point and intercept read from the load line.
k_n change observed on the load line.
